 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants, seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. The brief facts of the case are that on 01.05.2011 at about 6-00 PM, one Manchegowda (pedestrian) was walking on the left side on Maddur- Malavalli Main Road, at C.A. Kere Gate.

At that time, a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03/HA-9025 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed him, due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and thereafter during the treatment period, he succumbed to the injuries.
The claimants being the wife and children of the deceased, have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.

4. The Tribunal after considering oral and documentary evidence on record, has awarded a total compensation of Rs.40,000/-, under the following heads :
Sl.No. Particulars Amount  (in.Rs.)
 1. Loss of consortium Rs.15,000-00
2 . Love and affection 15,000-00  3. Transportation of dead body 10,000-00  and funeral expenses
Being aggrieved by the lesser quantum of compensation, the present appeal is filed.
6. In the present case, the deceased was 80 years old man, died in the accident.
The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest at 6% from the date of petition till the date of realization, which is meager one.
Therefore, the compensation is to be re-determined on the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and by this Court.
The claimant No.1 is wife of the deceased, claimant Nos.2 to 5 are the children of the deceased and claimant No.1, they are major.

Hence, claimant No.1 is entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'
7.
It is stated that the deceased was running a petty shop for his livelihood.

Legally and in all aspect,
the wife was depending on the deceased for her survival, even though the deceased was old aged.

Therefore, claimant No.1 - wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency' and other claimants are entitled for loss of consortium, loss of estate etc.,

sentences.text: Claimant No.1 being the wife of the deceased died during pendency of the appeal.

Just because,
the wife died during the pendency of the appeal, her right does not extinguish, had the appeal been disposed off during the life time of claimant No.1 (wife), then, she would have entitled to receive the compensation.
Therefore, just because the claimant No.1 (wife of deceased) died during pendency of the appeal, her right does not extinguish.

The claim petition does not abate and right to sue survives to her heirs and legal representatives, which is held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Kahlon @

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Jasmail Singh Kahlon reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 691.
9.
The accident was caused in the year 2011.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.6,500/- p.m., as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The claimant No.1-wife was depending on the earnings of the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd of his income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenditure.
The appropriate multiplier applicable to his age group is '5'.

Therefore, the 'Loss of Dependency' would be calculated as under:
Rs.6,500 x 2/3 x 5 x 12 = Rs.2,60,000/-
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.2,60,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.
10.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards 'Loss of Consortium' and Rs.15,000/-
towards 'Love and affection', which is on the lesser side.
The loss of consortium and loss of love and affection are more or less having similar connotations.
There are totally five claimants who are wife and children of the deceased.
Therefore, they are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the claimants are entitled for a total sum of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head 'Loss of consortium'.
11.

The cost incurred on account of transportation of dead body, funeral and ritual expenses, and towards loss of estate is modified by granting a sum of Rs.15,000/- The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards 'Loss of estate'.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is granted towards 'Loss of estate'.
12.
Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,90,000/- as against Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The break-up is as under:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  01 Loss of dependency 2,60,000-00
02 Loss of consortium 2,00,000-00
03 Transportation of dead 15,000-00  body, funeral & ritual  expenses and loss of estate

04 Loss of Estate 15,000-00  Total compensation Rs.4,90,000-00 Smt. Ningamma vs Sri. Niranjan Kumar on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15407486/
4 13.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.40,000/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,90,000/-.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,50,000/- (Rs.4,90,000 - Rs.40,000/-) along with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.3395/2011 dated 16.11.2012 by the VII Addl.

Small Causes Judge, Member, MACT-3, Bangalore, is hereby modified and appellants/claimants are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.4,50,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iii. Costs made easy.
Ordered accordingly.
v. The other observations and findings including the apportionment of compensation are kept in tact.
